correctness.rationale: At zero-delay update the vector (x_t,x_{t-1}) resets to (-x_t/5,x_t), giving a rank-one reset and an exact positive renewal process indexed by gaps between D=0 events. The renewal kernel has b_1=p/25 and b_{L+1}=(1-p)^2*p^(L-1)*(e1^T A1^L v)^2, v=(-1/5,1). A rational resolvent for the A1 symmetric moment map gives 1-B(1)=24*(432p^3-156p^2-305p+125)/[25*(6p-5)*(36p^2+35p+25)] below 5/6, with B infinite above. Aperiodic positive-kernel renewal theorem gives exponential decay for B(1)<1, nonzero critical renewal level when =1 and exponential growth when >1; last-zero decomposition transfers to E[x_t^2]. Independently recomputed symbolic 6x6 moment transfer determinant -24*cubic/3125, B mass rational, 3 real roots including 0.4267763163 and 0.7912257351, positive Lyapunov matrix at p=1/2. All-p claim rests on renewal argument rather than finitely many simulated delays.

originality.rationale: Dutta et al. 2018 full original PMLR text gives step-size-restricted sufficient bounds for asynchronous stochastic gradient descent and a conditional freshness p0; its Theorem 3 does not classify Markov-persistence p at overrelaxed step 6/5. Arjevani--Shamir--Srebro 2020 full original text fixes delay tau (rather than Markov switching) and supplies complexity estimates via generating functions, not this exact two-crossover mean-square region. General Markov-jump moment transfer criteria are known and not claimed new. A separate indexed randomized Gauss--Seidel delay-law result concerns iid bounded delay and another algorithm, so it does not entail this correlated two-state cubic. Unindexed equivalent jump-linear-system examples remain an originality risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed general Markov jump-linear model may give a parametrically equivalent stability region with this exact scalar update, not found.

value.rationale: All p share the same 1/2 fresh-gradient marginal but correlation alone changes the exact stability regime twice. The sharp rational cubic frontier is a precise counterexample to explanations based solely on expected staleness and a motivated stochastic-optimization stability test. It is not a queue-system universal law or an arbitrary one-shot algebra identity.

final_claim: For scalar delayed gradient descent x_{t+1}=x_t-(6/5)x_{t-D_t} on f=x^2/2 with stationary symmetric Markov D in {0,1}, persistence probability p∈(0,1), deterministic x_-1=x_0 nonzero, mean-square error decays geometrically exactly for p between the two positive roots of 432p^3-156p^2-305p+125; at roots it has positive liminf, otherwise grows exponentially despite identical marginal delay law.
